title: Yeast stress response: biology, metabolic consequences, and current model scope
scope: A representative Saccharomyces cerevisiae mechanism map, not an exhaustive pathway inventory or a kinetic model.
interpretation: Stressor, molecular sensor, signaling kinase, transcription factor, metabolic effector, and population outcome are different roles.
The referenced pathway table is a historical yeast-GEM 9.0.2 catalogue. Gene-reaction associations must be queried separately in each supplied model.
GPR associations, including enzyme-accounting reactions, do not establish signaling dynamics, induction, repression, or a measured regulatory coupling.
A named panel programme is usually a phenomenological dose-response entry. It is not automatically a mechanistic ODE or a state learned by the current student.
The in-silico teacher/student aggregates are explicitly synthetic proxies. The separate published-HOG parameter fit does not turn those aggregates into identified biological pathways.
Additional entities extend the conceptual map and are not assigned quantitative kinetics or inferred coverage without separate evidence.

branches.title: Peroxide and oxidative stress
branches.signal: Gpx3/Orp1-Ybp1 relay; Yap1 oxidation and nuclear retention; Skn7 cooperation
branches.regulators: Yap1/Skn7 are regulatory factors; antioxidant reactions are downstream chemistry.
branches.effectors: Catalase, peroxiredoxins, thioredoxin and glutathione recycling; NADPH demand
branches.scope_note: Only the H2O2 reporter route has an optional mechanistic panel adapter; other oxidants cannot inherit its dose-entry law automatically.

branches.title: ER folding and unfolded protein response
branches.input: Disulfide disruption, glycosylation defects, secretory protein load
branches.signal: Ire1 activation and unconventional HAC1 mRNA splicing
branches.regulators: Hac1 induces ER folding, quality-control and membrane programmes.
branches.effectors: Kar2/Pdi1 folding machinery, ER-associated degradation and ER membrane demand
branches.scope_note: The current UPR-named latent coordinate is a synthetic aggregate, not a learned Ire1/Hac1 splice-state model. DTT and tunicamycin require distinct entry assumptions.

branches.title: Heat and cytosolic proteotoxic stress
branches.input: Temperature shifts, misfolded proteins, damaged proteins
branches.signal: Chaperone availability and Hsf1 activity; proteasome feedback through Rpn4
branches.regulators: Hsf1 and Rpn4 are distinct programmes with cross-regulation, not one generic stress factor.
branches.effectors: Chaperones, disaggregation, proteasomal turnover; ATP and amino-acid costs
branches.scope_note: Catalogue entries and optional chaperone-cost adapters exist; the current student does not learn a heat-shock or proteasome signaling state.

branches.title: Osmotic and ionic stress
branches.input: Osmolarity changes, NaCl, sorbitol; ionic toxicity is an additional load
branches.signal: Sln1 phosphorelay and Sho1-associated branch converge on Pbs2-Hog1
branches.regulators: Hog1 is a MAP kinase, not a transcription factor; Hot1/Sko1 and other targets execute transcriptional output.
branches.effectors: Glycerol synthesis and retention, Fps1 gating, turgor recovery and ion transport
branches.scope_note: A separate published WT osmoadaptation SBML route now supplies Hog1/glycerol/Fps1/turgor dynamics, and a measured-data fit estimates the activation balance conditional on the other source parameters. It is not the default synthetic student's state or a generic panel reporter adapter. Upstream Sln1/Sho1-Pbs2 signaling is lumped, ionic toxicity and sorbitol transfer are not established, and Gpd1 capacity scaling is not a learned glycerol flux-allocation law.

branches.title: Cell-wall integrity and mechanical stress
branches.input: Wall damage, mechanical strain, membrane-wall perturbation
branches.regulators: Rlm1 and associated transcriptional programmes; Rho1 also has a structural glucan-synthase role.
branches.effectors: Glucan, chitin and mannan synthesis; wall remodeling and cross-linking
branches.scope_note: A biomass requirement or Rho1 GPR association does not implement the CWI cascade or stress-induced wall remodeling.

branches.title: Carbon sensing and energy allocation
branches.input: Glucose availability, carbon-source transitions and energy demand
branches.signal: Gpr1/Ras-cAMP-PKA and Snf1-AMPK are distinct nutrient/energy pathways
branches.regulators: PKA-sensitive stress/growth programmes; Snf1-linked Mig1 relief and Adr1/Cat8 output
branches.effectors: Carbon-source utilization, respiratory allocation, reserve mobilization and growth programmes
branches.scope_note: cAMP synthesis/degradation reactions do not create glucose sensing, PKA dynamics or Snf1 regulation. Low growth alone is not an authoritative stress label.

branches.title: Nitrogen and extracellular amino acids
branches.input: Nitrogen quality/availability and extracellular amino-acid signals
branches.signal: TORC1 nutrient integration; separate SPS Ssy1-Ptr3-Ssy5 sensing branch
branches.regulators: Gln3/Gat1 nitrogen catabolite regulation; SPS-dependent Stp1/Stp2 processing
branches.effectors: Amino-acid uptake/utilization, translation allocation and autophagy
branches.scope_note: SPS is not a quorum-sensing system. The nitrogen catalogue entry does not supply SPS or TORC1 kinetic states.

branches.title: General stress versus growth programmes
branches.input: Integrated nutrient, damage and energy signals
branches.signal: PKA/TOR/Sch9 and pathway-specific cross-talk regulate different transcriptional outputs
branches.regulators: Induced ESR through Msn2/Msn4; ribosome-biogenesis repression includes Dot6/Tod6 and other growth regulators
branches.effectors: Protective proteins and reserve metabolism versus ribosome/translation allocation
branches.scope_note: Induction and repression are not interchangeable. A generic growth-retention scalar is not a learned ESR/RiBi regulatory model.

branches.title: Acid entry and cytosolic pH
branches.input: External acidity, weak-acid speciation and membrane permeability
branches.signal: Cytosolic proton/anion load; weak-acid regulatory branches include Haa1 and War1
branches.regulators: Acid-specific transcription and export require their own regulatory representation.
branches.effectors: Pma1 plasma-membrane pumping, V-ATPase organelle acidification and acid-anion export
branches.scope_note: Pma1/V-ATPase are effectors, not receptor-level sensors. Haa1/War1 are expansion targets; their kinetics are not supplied by the acid-balance equations or this catalogue.

branches.title: Alkaline pH and calcium signaling
branches.input: Alkaline conditions, ion imbalance and calcium transients
branches.signal: Rim21-associated sensing and ESCRT/Rim proteolysis; Ca2+/calmodulin-calcineurin branch
branches.regulators: Processed Rim101 and calcineurin-responsive Crz1 have distinct roles.
branches.effectors: Ion transport, Ena pumps, calcium homeostasis and cell-surface adaptation
branches.scope_note: Rim101 is chiefly an alkaline-pH response branch, not a generic low-pH sensor. Ion transport does not establish calcium-signaling dynamics.

branches.title: Oxygen, membrane state and ethanol
branches.input: Oxygen limitation, sterol availability and ethanol-associated damage
branches.signal: Heme/sterol-responsive regulation; ethanol can perturb membrane, folding and redox states
branches.regulators: Hap1/Rox1/Upc2 plus condition-dependent HSR, CWI and oxidative responses
branches.effectors: Respiration, sterol/lipid composition, membrane transport and protective metabolism
branches.scope_note: Oxygen constraints and ethanol as a carbon substrate are not an ethanol-toxicity signaling model. No dedicated universal ethanol receptor is assumed.

branches.title: Metals, sulfur and chemical defense
branches.input: Metal deficiency/excess, sulfur availability and xenobiotics
branches.regulators: Aft1/Aft2, Mac1/Cup2, Zap1, Met4 complexes and Pdr1/Pdr3 are distinct programmes.
branches.effectors: Uptake/sequestration, thiol metabolism, cofactor supply and substrate-specific efflux
branches.scope_note: One metal or efflux reaction cannot stand in for all metal or drug responses; substrates, cofactors and regulatory magnitudes need separate definitions.

branches.title: DNA integrity and organelle feedback
branches.input: DNA damage, replication stress and mitochondrial dysfunction
branches.regulators: Rfx1/Crt1-mediated dNTP regulation and Rtg1/Rtg3-dependent metabolic responses
branches.effectors: dNTP supply, repair, cell-cycle control and metabolic redistribution
branches.scope_note: Nucleotide synthesis reactions do not simulate checkpoints, repair lesions or organelle signaling.

branches.title: Production burden, plasmids and populations
branches.input: Recombinant expression, secretion, plasmid replication and segregation
branches.signal: Resource demand and proteostasis feedback; copy number and population composition are separate variables
branches.regulators: Energy/nutrient/folding programmes can respond; plasmid loss is not itself a transcription factor.
branches.effectors: Growth, producer fraction, product pools, genotype stability and viability
branches.scope_note: The current burden coordinate is delayed memory of two imposed stresses. It is not a full expression-allocation, plasmid-copy or population model. Separate burden/population approximations exist elsewhere.

branches.title: Community behavior and additional nutrient axes
branches.input: Adhesion/community context, extracellular metabolites and phosphate limitation
branches.signal: Flocculation/filamentation signaling and the PHO nutrient programme are additional branches
branches.regulators: FLO-associated regulation and Pho4/Pho80-Pho85 are extension targets, not generic SPS output.
branches.effectors: Aggregation, biofilm/filamentation, nutrient acquisition and altered measurement geometry
branches.scope_note: These are explicitly unparameterized extensions. Quorum-like effects are strain/condition dependent; aggregation also changes how OD and fluorescence should be interpreted.

shared_feedbacks: ATP/GTP, NADPH and amino-acid demand connect signaling outputs to metabolic resource constraints.
Damage, repair, osmotic volume, intracellular pH and organelle state feed back into signaling; a one-way stress-to-flux arrow omits these loops.
Transcript induction, protein abundance, enzyme activity and metabolic flux are distinct quantities with different delays and units.
Growth dilution, viability, producer fraction, aggregation and fluorophore chemistry affect observations and must not be mistaken for stress labels.
missing_quantitative_layers: Condition-specific activation, adaptation, localization and feedback kinetics for the broad signaling map
Gene-specific induction and repression with resource-consistent translation and enzyme turnover
Independent observation models that make additional stress states identifiable
Validated stress-to-metabolic-control laws rather than the synthetic teacher's fixed controller
Coupled damage, repair, viability and population dynamics beyond the synthesis-only reference protocol
